newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal PM to visit Britain to seek investment.
newsitem.headline: Nepal PM to visit Britain to seek investment.

text.p: Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba starts a three-day visit to Britain on Sunday to seek investment for his country's aid-dependent economy, Nepal's foreign minister said on Thursday.
"We will also tell them about our economic policy and request for more British investment in different sectors, including hydro-power, tea and tourism," Prakash Chandra Lohani told Reuters.
Deuba is scheduled to meet British Prime Minister John Major, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and Defence Secretary Michael Portillo during the visit.
Britain is a major aid donor to Nepal, one of the world's 10 poorest countries.
Initially, British assistance to Nepal was half grant and half soft-term lending. In 1976, London decided to make all its future aid to Nepal a non-refundable grant.
During his visit, Deuba will address the Confederation of British Industries and the London School of Economics.
Nepal's trade deficit with Britain was $12.9 million in 1995-96, a 48.5 percent increase from $8.7 million in 1994-95.
But officials said overall balance of payments was in the black because of the income from more than 27,000 British tourists and remittances from the Nepal's Gurkha soldiers in the British army.
